provenance.claim_boundary: One H200, public source-derived compact Gated-MLA factorization versus an independent materialized float64 reference on the complete synthetic FP32 ordinary/stress grid. No K3 checkpoint, production kernel, timing, memory, training stability, or serving claim.

fixture.generator: torch.Generator(device='cpu').manual_seed(seed), torch.randn float32 in the listed source-tensor order; the producer retains every generated source tensor
fixture.case_order: shapes, then regimes, then seeds in listed order
fixture.source_recipe: Use the source tensor shapes, Gaussian scales, and fixed outliers in build_base_sources from gmla_public_parity_kernel.py, with every case's storage_dtype=float32. Apply regime scales to input_x, both incoming record tensors, gate_weight, and output_weight respectively before either arm. Do not change parameters after observing results.
fixture.mask: Each request attends to its own incoming records and current tokens through its own current position, including self; no cross-request records are visible.
fixture.accepted_prefix: incoming_lengths in the shape object are the accepted prefix lengths; the same records are used in both arms

numeric_policy.gate: Compute channel gate once in FP32 from identical source input and gate weights, then pass those exact retained FP32 values to both arms; compare compact and materialized attention output and post-gate final output.
numeric_policy.quantile_rule: linear interpolation at (n-1)*q over sorted finite coordinate errors
numeric_policy.pass_gate: For both attention and final outputs, all coordinates and metrics must be finite and either maximum absolute error <= 0.002 or relative RMS error <= 0.001.
numeric_policy.nonfinite_policy: Retain each nonfinite or exception disposition and count all nonfinite candidate, reference, gate, and metric coordinates; any such case fails. No failed or unsupported cell is replaced.
